questions.question: How do floating plants differ from submerged plants?
questions.solution_html:
• Floating plants and submerged plants differ mainly in their position in water, structure
  • and function.
  • Floating plants: Float on the surface of the water, Roots may hang freely in water or
  • may be reduced, Leaves are exposed to air and receive direct sunlight, Help in
  • shading the aquarium, reducing algae, and absorbing excess nutrients , Examples
  • duckweed and water lettuce
  • Submerged plants: Grow completely under water, Roots are usually anchored in the
  • substrate, Leaves are adapted to live underwater (thin, flexible), Play a major role in
  • oxygen production through Photosynthesis and provide shelter for fish , Examples
  • Hydrilla and Vallisneria
